mutant_analysis.coverage_note: Both mutants are caught at the TypeScript compile-time level via the typed fixture declarations in the test file. vitest runtime does not catch either mutant because: (1) esbuild strips types at transpile time; (2) the runtime objects are plain literals that never contained `has_more`, and `count` is absent from cursorPageNoCount so `.count` is `undefined` regardless. The TypeScript type annotations on the fixture constants act as the compile-time specification — they would be caught by a `tsc --noEmit` CI gate (or equivalent `mix letflow.check.test` front-end type check step if one exists).
mutant_analysis.gap_identified: TC-ISS0821-03 uses `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(cursorPageNoCount, 'has_more')` to check that `has_more` is absent at runtime. This assertion would only fail if the fixture was constructed WITH `has_more` set (e.g. if a future developer writes `{ items, next_cursor, has_more: false }`). The deeper compile-time guarantee is provided by the `expectTypeOf` pattern (vitest built-in), which would be a stronger upgrade. Current coverage relies on TypeScript's structural assignment check on the typed fixture, which is caught by tsc but transparent to vitest runtime.

iss_0822_static_analysis.rationale: The ISS-0822 regression is structural: the SPA route `{ path: 'admin/modules', element: <ProcessModulesPage /> }` was active while the backend router was never mounted. The fix is removal of that route. Static analysis confirming the route is gone (not just hidden) is the appropriate coverage form — a vitest test asserting router structure would be fragile and need updating on every route change. The two checks above confirm: (1) no route declaration matching 'admin/modules' exists; (2) ProcessModulesPage is not imported as a live symbol. Both matches are comments-only (explanatory tombstones for the removed code).
